stem: A Massachusetts entity holds a provisional outsourcing facility registration because it had not been inspected by the FDA in the two years before its application. It has compounded a batch of sterile preparations and wants to ship them to a hospital in the Commonwealth while it waits for the inspection. May it?

choices.text: Yes, because the provisional registration authorises it to operate as a facility.
Yes, because the shipment stays inside the Commonwealth.
Yes, provided the receiving hospital records the provisional status.
No, because a provisional holder is barred from compounding until inspected.
No, because a provisional holder is permitted to compound but not to supply.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 21.03(3) provides that an entity with a provisional outsourcing facility registration MAY COMPOUND sterile drug preparations but MAY NOT DISTRIBUTE OR DISPENSE a sterile drug preparation within or outside the Commonwealth until it has been inspected by the FDA and has received a Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration. The permission and the prohibition sit in the same sentence.

choice_analysis.A: The registration authorises production, not supply.
choice_analysis.B: The prohibition covers supply within and outside the Commonwealth alike.
choice_analysis.C: No recording by the recipient cures the prohibition.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: compounding yes, distribution or dispensing no.

related_facts: A non-resident outsourcing facility cannot hold a provisional registration at all
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a registration that permits production as permitting supply of what is produced.

reasoning_steps: Read the permission and the prohibition in the same provision
Note that the geographic reach of the prohibition is both ways
Identify the two conditions that lift it
